hypotheses.statement: Heater has positive steady-state gain: higher constant u yields higher equilibrium y.
Step response has appreciable lag/delay: y takes tens to hundreds of seconds to approach equilibrium.
No large dead zone: even u=0.3-0.5 produces a clear rise compared to u=0.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0-0.1 due to heat loss.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear in u across 0 to 1.
Constant u near 0.5 holds y near target 0.5 at equilibrium.
Sensor noise and short-term fluctuations are small (<~0.01) compared to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag: a first mid-level hold discriminates heating vs no response and measures rise rate and curvature needed for all later control design.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case level = 0.1681 + 0.006*0.5*200 = 0.7681, which stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin, using current y=0.1681 and no decay or lag credit.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater with lag is correct, y will rise monotonically from ~0.17 toward ~0.3-0.5 over 200 s with initially small slope that grows then flattens; end value clearly above start value and final slope still positive if not fully settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain, lag, decay at u=0, linearity, steady-state input for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved; at least three experiments are required before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: hold mid power 0.5 for 200 s to measure heating direction, rate and lag.

hypotheses.statement: Heater has positive steady-state gain: higher constant u yields higher equilibrium y.
Step response has appreciable lag: time constant order 150-250 s (~200 s) to approach equilibrium.
No large dead zone: even u=0.3-0.5 produces a clear rise compared to u=0.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0.12-0.20 due to heat loss.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear in u across 0 to 0.5 with slope ~1.0-1.4 per unit u.
Constant u near 0.5 holds y near target 0.5 at equilibrium.
Sensor noise and short-term fluctuations are small (<~0.01) compared to control band width 0.05.
Steady-state input needed to hold y=0.5 was ~0.24-0.29 before change, because u=0.3 settled near ~0.55 with flat slope while u=0.4 and 0.5 exceeded 0.5 while still rising.
Change is weaker actuator: same u>0 gives smaller rise, but u=0 cooling rate/ambient (~0.12-0.20) and delay (~15-30 s) unchanged.
Change is faster outflow / increased heat loss: fall at u=0 is faster than in E2 and equilibrium for same u and ambient are lower.
Change is slower response: increased deadtime/time constant, delay from command change to first response >50-60 s vs ~20 s in E1/E2.
Change is sensor offset/noise: true thermal dynamics unchanged but readings show persistent ~-0.07 to -0.10 bias and/or larger negative dips.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0 cooling rate/ambient and initial delay are unchanged, which discriminates increased loss vs weakened heater vs longer delay vs sensor bias and fixes new feedforward hold power and integral time.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is current y 0.4109 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.4109, well below soft limit 0.85; u=0 cannot heat, only cools, with large margin to hard cutoff.
proposal.expected_observation: If increased-loss (C2) is leading, y will hold/flat or creep up for ~15-30 s responding to in-transit prior ~0.47 command, then fall monotonically and faster than E2, dropping >0.10 in first 100 s from ~0.41 toward <0.20 by 300-400 s with slope ~-0.002 to -0.003/s early flattening late. If actuator-only weakening (C1) is true, fall rate and ambient will match E2 (~-0.001 to -0.002/s early, ambient 0.12-0.20). Flat >60 s before falling would indicate longer delay (C3); no fall with persistent ~-0.08 bias would favor sensor offset (C4).
proposal.readiness_justification: No after-change experiments completed yet; closed-loop rise of u from 0.28 to 0.47 with y stuck at 0.46 to 0.41 confounds gain loss vs outflow vs delay vs sensor bias, so not ready; this u=0 hold will resolve delay, cooling rate and ambient before testing heating gain.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure cooling rate and delay on changed plant.

submission.machine_card: Heater, positive gain, self-draining to room. u in [0,1] power, y in [0,1] temp (0=15C,1=75C). No deadzone: u=0.3-0.5 clearly heats. Ambient at u=0: ~0.12-0.20, mean ~0.17 (E2 decay 0.587 to 0.152 in 480s). Gain: near target ~0.78-0.80 (E8: u=0.25 holds 0.508 flat slope -0.0003; E7: u=0.30 holds 0.547 flat 0.0002; delta 0.039/0.05=0.78). Low-end secant ~1.35 ((0.508-0.17)/0.25). Hold for y=0.5 ~0.24 (interp: (0.5-0.17)/1.352=0.244; between settled points 0.25-0.010=0.24). E1 u=0.5 rises 0.174 to 0.553 in 200s still rising +0.0007/s, equilibrium >0.6. E3 u=0.4 rises to 0.527 still rising. Lag: first-order tau ~150-200s, no pure delay; rise/cool over 200-400s. Speed: typical 0.001-0.002/s, worst-case bound 0.006/s. Noise: base +/-0.015-0.02 plus frequent one-sample negative outliers -0.05 to -0.08 (E1 0.3884, E3 0.1923/0.3406, E7 0.4883, E8 0.4818/0.4839). Must filter, do not chase spikes. True y hidden; overshoot unseen in y still scored.
submission.design_rationale: Plant is first-order self-draining heater, tau~150s, positive gain, no deadzone. Near target gain K~0.78 from two settled points (0.25,0.508 in E8 and 0.30,0.547 in E7); low-end secant gain 1.35 from (0,0.17 in E2) to (0.25,0.508). Interpolated hold for 0.5 is 0.244. Use feedforward 0.244 + PI correcting residual. Kp=0.85 gives closed-loop tau~83s for settling <300s without aggressive saturation; Ki=0.009 (Ti~94s) removes offset in ~200s. Tf=14s low-pass + innovation clamp 0.035+0.004*dt rejects single-sample -0.05 to -0.08 negative spikes that cannot be physical (max rate 0.006/s) while adding only 14s lag vs 150s plant. Integral authority +-0.15 covers FF error up to 0.15, far larger than observed 0.05 uncertainty, but clamped to prevent windup; integration frozen when |e|>0.15 and when saturated to avoid cold-start overshoot. Umax=0.65 guarantees equilibrium <0.83 below soft 0.85/hard 0.9; rate limit 0.05/s suppresses chatter without slowing plant.
